user.title: Utility cost tracker
user.description: A site is something you get one bill for, such as the electricity of your home. Once it's added, open it to add the prices and fees from the bill.

data_description.name: Such as Home electricity.
data_description.utility: The site gets the usual cost elements for it, such as Energy and Transfer for electricity. You can rename or remove them later.
data_description.consumption_entity: The sensor with the meter's running total, such as the energy bought in kWh or the water used in m³.
data_description.factor: The meter reading is multiplied by this before any price. Leave it at 1 unless the reading needs converting, such as gas from m³ to kWh.
data_description.periods: Every cost gets a sensor for each period you choose.
data_description.price_unit: Whether you type prices in your currency or in its hundredths, such as cents per kWh. The price sensors show prices in the same unit. Costs are always in the currency set in Home Assistant.
data_description.hundredth_symbol: Such as c, öre or p. Only used when prices are in hundredths.

reconfigure.title: Utility cost tracker
reconfigure.description: Changes take effect right away. What has been counted so far stays.

user.title: Cost element
user.description: A part of the bill with its own tax rate, such as Energy or Transfer.

data_description.tax: Such as value added tax. Each item says whether it's taxed. Leave it at 0 if there's no tax.

menu_options.sensor: Price per unit from a sensor

constant.title: Fixed price per unit
constant.description: Such as the seller's margin, the electricity tax, a transfer price or water per m³.

data_description.taxed: The cost element's tax rate is added to this.
data_description.includes_tax: Turn this on if you're typing the price with tax, the way your contract or bill shows it.
data_description.timing: Choose at other times for a price that applies whenever none of the element's time-limited prices do, such as night transfer next to a day price.
data_description.consumption_entity: Leave it empty to use the site's meter. Pick a sub-meter, such as a car charger's, to price only what it measures.
data_description.factor: The consumption is multiplied by this before pricing, such as 0.9 if wastewater is billed on 90 % of the water. Otherwise leave it at 1.

sensor.title: Price per unit from a sensor
sensor.description: Such as a spot price. The multiplier converts the sensor's value to the unit of your other prices, and the addition adds a fixed part to it, such as a margin.

data_description.multiplier: Converts the sensor's value to the unit you type prices in, such as 100 when the sensor's price is in the currency and your other prices are in hundredths. Otherwise leave it at 1.
data_description.addend: Added after the multiplier. Otherwise leave it at 0.
data_description.taxed: The cost element's tax rate is added to this.
data_description.includes_tax: Turn this on if the sensor's price, and the addition, already include tax.
data_description.timing: Choose at other times for a price that applies whenever none of the element's time-limited prices do, such as night transfer next to a day price.
data_description.consumption_entity: Leave it empty to use the site's meter. Pick a sub-meter, such as a car charger's, to price only what it measures.
data_description.factor: The consumption is multiplied by this before pricing. Otherwise leave it at 1.

fixed_fee.title: Fixed fee
fixed_fee.description: Such as a monthly basic fee. It's added in full at the start of each period, however much you use, and shows in the sensors of that period and longer ones.

data_description.price: In your currency, also when prices are typed in hundredths. Use a negative amount for a credit.
data_description.taxed: The cost element's tax rate is added to this.
data_description.includes_tax: Turn this on if you're typing the amount with tax, the way your contract or bill shows it.

window.title: When it applies
window.description: The price applies between these times, on the days and in the months you choose.

data_description.end: An end before the start runs over midnight, such as 22:00 to 07:00. The same time for both means all day.
data_description.weekdays: Leave it empty for every day.
data_description.months: Leave it empty for every month.

data_description.includes_tax: Turn this on if you're typing the price with tax, the way your contract or bill shows it.
data_description.timing: Choose at other times for a price that applies whenever none of the element's time-limited prices do.
data_description.consumption_entity: Leave it empty to use the site's meter.

error.includes_untaxed: A price can only include tax if it's taxed.

abort.no_elements: Add a cost element first. Every item belongs to one.
